summary: Use Debian 13 stable OVMF for new Nex Core ISOs and retire the sid-only firmware package path.

guide.reason: New guest Secure Boot templates use Debian stable OVMF without the 2023 Microsoft CAs; the VM guide now states the boot-media limit and the edit guide distinguishes saved VM state from a host firmware package change.

api.reason: The ISO package selection changes no Controller, Core or client API; Core continues to discover the same libvirt enrolled-keys firmware descriptor and OVMF paths.

roadmap.reason: The stable-firmware switch reopens guest Secure Boot compatibility acceptance for the next ISO.

state.reason: The package source change adds no pool setting, VM identity or Controller-owned state; the selected firmware package is installed on each Core host by the ISO.

verification.method: bash installer/check.sh passed; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passed 399 tests, including storage packaging and source-bundle checks; bash -n installer/build.sh installer/late-install.sh and Python syntax checks passed. The exact Debian stable ovmf 2025.02-8+deb13u1 package was extracted and its enrolled firmware descriptor, paths, and two Microsoft 2011 db certificate fingerprints were inspected using virt-fw-vars and OpenSSL in a disposable Debian trixie container. python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree, repository privacy, website check/build and diff checks passed. A new full ISO build, matching source-bundle inspection, disposable install, fresh signed-guest boot and existing-guest NVRAM compatibility remain unrun.
verification.limits: No new ISO or host was built or installed in this change; historical sid-OVMF artifact evidence cannot verify stable-OVMF behavior.
